answer: Escrowed compute decay. Each agent identity must post a cipher-keyed escrow that unlocks only after it produces sustained useful work; idle or duplicate identities forfeit a rising fraction. The cost curve steepens with cluster similarity, so mass-registering near-identical agents pays a pigment-like markup at registration and a ridge of escalating forfeitures over time. An attacker's per-identity cost compounds faster than the number of identities they add, making large sybil farms economically self-defeating.
